title: [recoverability] Restore drill 3, the transcript archive: restore-drill --only transcripts restores the archive alone from the newest bundle chain into its own folder, judges every file by the newest record's size and sha256 without reading live, refuses under the 40 GB floor, removes only its own folder after its identity and file-type checks, records backup.drilled.transcripts alone; its unit and timer; the U1 row
prompt:
Spawn, objective 200 [recoverability], after 186 (the owner's order of 2026-11-14 18:43: restores passed must read 6 of 6, guardrail U1; restore drill 3 of the owner's four; the lead's brief and choice (A) of 2026-11-15): the transcript archive's own restore drill. The off-host copy of the transcript archive is restored on its own every day, judged by its own record, and nothing original is ever opened.

The archive's off-host copy is the daily bundle chain in R2 (sync/recovery.md; since 2026-11-12 every transcript is in each full bundle). Only the combined `spawn backup restore-drill` restores it today, and that drill also reads live and stays uninstalled until 152 and 154. 186 drills the mission repositories alone (`--only missions`); nothing drills the transcripts alone. The store (`spawn store`) is not a backup of the archive yet (a 14-file sample), so it is not this drill.

Base: live main 154278fd (186 landed as b92d1289; 174, 190 and 194 since).

Read first:
- crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs: restore_drill, only_missions, run, fetch_missions and missions_members (186's pipe: gpg into tar -t, then tar -x of chosen names), restore_transcripts, judge_by_record, DrillDir;
- deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-missions.{service,timer} (186's unit and timer, which the new ones follow);
- deploy/backup/README.md, the drill sections.

What changes:
(1) `spawn backup restore-drill --only transcripts`:
   - `--only` takes missions or transcripts; anything else (repos, an empty value) exits 2 with nothing recorded. Without --only the drill is as before.
   - From each bundle of the newest chain it unpacks by name only `manifest.json` and the files under `transcripts/` (no directory, no `.` or `..` part, no name tar had to quote), through 186's pipe: the ciphertext fetched, decrypted into tar -t, its sha256 the record's before anything is extracted, then tar -x of those names alone. No repository bundle is unpacked.
   - Every unpacked tree must hold only directories and regular files, else the drill fails (a symlink in a bundle is never followed).
   - It restores the chain's slices into its own folder (restore_transcripts) and judges each file by the newest record alone: the size the record names, and its sha256 in the record's `transcripts.sha256`. A record bundled before objective 149 names no sha256 and fails it. It never reads live: the archive, ~/.claude, the session backups and every path outside its folder stay unopened.
   - Free space: before it fetches anything it refuses, with one line naming the floor, exit 2 and nothing recorded, when the chain's ciphertext and slices plus the newest record's files (from the records) would leave the folder's file system under the floor: `SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_FLOOR_MB`, default 40960 (40 GB).
   - It records `backup.drilled.transcripts` alone (the existing record and schema), prints counts and the record's counts line ("<k> of <n> files as the newest record's sha256"), never a transcript's text. Exit 0 passed, 1 failed, 2 cannot run.
(2) Deleting (the deleter review's questions, for the reviewer):
   - Reach: only its own folder, `<parent>/spawn-restore-drill-<pid>-<hex>` (DrillDir), made by this run with mode 700 under `--into` (default /data/tmp; never under $HOME, $SPAWN_LIVE or the workspace root, symlinks resolved). The files in it are copies (the owner's 11-14 10:16 rule: copies may go; originals never).
   - In use: nothing else reads or writes the folder during the run; the drill alone made it, and its name is its own.
   - Scope: it is removed by its literal path only after DrillDir's identity check (the parent it was made in, a drill's name, still a directory and the same device and inode) and only when every entry under it is a directory or a regular file. Anything else fails the drill and leaves the folder, said. --keep leaves it.
(3) The owner's part:
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-transcripts.service: `spawn backup restore-drill --only transcripts` with the bundle unit's environment (as the missions unit), Nice 15, idle I/O, MemoryMax 1G, 1 h; exit 1 and 2 not retried.
   - deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-transcripts.timer: daily 06:15. Installed disabled; enabled after the lead's supervised first run.
   - deploy/backup/README.md: the drill, its install, and the U1 recovery-table row {"name": "transcripts", "unit": "spawn-backup-restore-drill-transcripts.service"} (the Core lines file's recoverability.drills, an owner config change made after landing).
   - rsi/scenarios/200.sh (new); rsi/scenarios/186.sh (5) refuses repos and an empty value, since transcripts is now taken.

What stays as it is: the combined drill and --only missions, their records and outputs; the bundle; the schema; the archive and every original (never opened).

Polled reads: none. The drill runs once a day.

Tests (spawn-cli backup::restore_drill):
- a_transcripts_only_drill_extracts_the_manifest_and_the_transcript_slices_alone (new): the names chosen from a listing; a listing without the manifest refused.
- the_drill_folder_is_plain_only_with_directories_and_regular_files (new): a symlink, even under a transcript's name, is refused and named.
- a_transcripts_only_drill_needs_its_bytes_above_the_floor (new): the bytes counted from the chain's records; the refusal line.
- a_missions_only_drill_extracts_the_manifest_and_the_repository_bundles_alone: kept, its --only cases now missions and transcripts taken, repos and '' refused.

Files: crates/spawn-cli/src/backup/restore_drill.rs, crates/spawn-cli/src/backup.rs and main.rs (usage, the module doc). The owner's: deploy/systemd/spawn-backup-restore-drill-transcripts.{service,timer} (new), deploy/backup/README.md, rsi/scenarios/200.sh (new), rsi/scenarios/186.sh.
Size (against 154278fd, rustfmt'd, without blank and comment lines): fleet 3 files, code +231 -64 (restore_drill.rs +229 -62, of which about 37 lines restore_drill's --only and parent blocks moved into resources_of and parent_of, unchanged, to keep restore_drill under clippy's 100 lines), doc comments 66, tests 72. Owner: 5 files, +1014 -7: 200.sh 926 (on 186.sh's harness), units 44, README +38 -2, 186.sh +6 -5.

Acceptance: rsi/scenarios/200.sh, black box on its own database, scratch HOME and GNUPGHOME, against 104's local R2 stand-in (186.sh's harness). The bundle and the first drill run as their units run them, the drill given --into a scratch parent. While a drill runs, the originals it must never open are mode 000: every file of the live archive, a transcript planted in the fake HOME (~/.claude/projects/), and another session's transcript planted beside the drill folders in the --into parent.
(1) The bundle unit's run records backup.bundled with a per-file sha256 (setup).
(2) The transcripts unit runs `restore-drill --only transcripts`, its timer names an OnCalendar. Its run passes (exit 0), says "--only transcripts" and "<n> of <n> files as the newest record's sha256", records exactly one backup.drilled.transcripts {ok true, reason "", the bundle's key and event, 0 mismatches} and no backup.drilled.missions, leaves nothing of its own in the parent, and every original and source is unchanged (path, size, sha256), mode 000 throughout.
(3) With --keep, the kept folder holds each of the record's transcripts under transcripts/ at the record's size and sha256, and no repository bundle.
(4) A transcript grown and a new one written, a second bundle: the drill over the newer chain passes, its record naming the new bundle, "<n> of <n>" its new count; the originals unchanged.
(5) With a floor no disk meets (SPAWN_BACKUP_DRILL_FLOOR_MB): exit 2, one line naming the floor, nothing recorded, nothing made in the parent.
(6) The newest bundle's stored bytes replaced by another ciphertext under the same passphrase: exit 1, the record ok false saying it decrypts to another sha256, nothing of its own left; with --keep nothing extracted.
(7) --into under the fake HOME or the workspace root, and --only repos or '': exit 2, nothing recorded.
(8) No secret (the backup passphrase, the R2 secret key) and no transcript's text in any record or output.
